summary.title: The Imposter's Handbook, Second Edition
summary.one_liner: A plain-English book by Rob Conery that fills computer science gaps (data structures, algorithms, and more) for self-taught developers preparing for technical interviews.
takeaways: Covers core CS fundamentals for self-taught developers: data structures, algorithms, Big-O, and state machines
Explains encoding, compression, and hashing so you can discuss technical decisions with more authority
Includes practical topics such as building databases, architecting complex systems, and Unix shell scripting
Second edition (2026 per the page timeline) is a full rewrite of the 2016 first edition, with 550 pages and 12 chapters
Sold as an instant download in EPUB (iPad or Kindle) or PDF after Stripe checkout
summary.summary: This is the sales page for The Imposter's Handbook, Second Edition, a 550-page book with 12 chapters written by Rob Conery for developers without formal CS degrees. The page lists the topics covered: data structures and algorithms, Big-O and state machines, encoding, compression and hashing, architecture options, database design, and Unix/shell scripting. It describes the book as a conversational, hand-drawn-doodle style text and says it is delivered as an immediate download in EPUB or PDF. The page is mostly marketing; it gives no price beyond the listing's $30, and the author's background and sales claims are self-reported.
